newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Branson balloon readied for around world flight.
newsitem.headline: Branson balloon readied for around world flight.

text.p: Technicians began on Monday to inflate the balloon that will take British tycoon Richard Branson on a record-beating flight around the world.
The huge green, yellow and red balloon, called Virgin Global Challenger, was hauled from a warehouse in a military air base in Marrakesh for the 12-hour countdown to take-off on Tuesday.

"The balloon, which will be filled by 1.1 million cubic feet of combined helium and hot air in a period of 12 hours starting from now, will climb to 30,000 feet over the snow capped Atlas mountains," Branson told reporters.
The balloon will fly over Algeria, Libya, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, Hong Kong, Japan, across the Pacific, America and the Atlantic before landing in England.
"No matter how long the trip will take to go round the world ...the main thing is to be the first person to do it," Branson told Reuters.
Branson, the flamboyant 46-year-old boss of the Virgin group of companies, seemed ready to make the attempt on Tuesday as the weather was promising.
Accompanied by his two co-pilots Per Lindstrand and Rory McCarthy, he said he was "confident that the trip will take place tomorrow at between 0630 and 0730 GMT".
This is the second time Branson has made an attempt on the world record. Bad weather forced the tycoon last year to put off his planned flight.
He said the total operation would cost sponsors between 1.5 ($2.5 million) and two million pounds.
The 194.8-foot balloon was constructed of fabric specifically designed for Branson's project.
The red-walled tourist city of Marrakesh has been chosen as the ideal launch pad as it is on the faster, southerly sub- tropical jet stream compared with the northern polar jet stream.
Speed is essential as the Branson team is racing against American balloonist Steve Fosset and a two-man team planning a launch from Switzerland.

Branson's three-man crew spent three days training in the new balloon in December and have been waiting since then for ideal weather in Morocco to take them on an 18-day balloon trip around the world.

The balloon flight is the latest in a series of record breaking attempts that have indulged Branson's taste for adventure while earning publicity for his businesses ranging from Virgin Atlantic Airways to financial services.
